findings.criterion: Bug is actually resolved: the reported defect (uv-launched MCP/gate python processes surviving harness exit and leaking ~10GB+) no longer reproduces
findings.detail: The ticket's acceptance criterion 3 requires that the tracked `.codex/config.toml` serena entry be removed so Codex no longer launches Serena against the full 31GB checkout (`--project-from-cwd`). The ticket's third comment states Gerrit change 2725 removes this entry and was 'merged as 53d18aad2ab9', but also notes 'ticket close stays blocked on that landing.' Reading `.codex/config.toml` in the current repository tree shows the `[mcp_servers.serena]` block is STILL PRESENT at lines 53–68 with `--project-from-cwd`. The Gerrit change has not landed in the current HEAD (f1dd41a8f09967dd60c7aefb5e43c6f62fa119af). The primary codebase fix — removing the tracked full-checkout Serena entry — is not present in the repository at the verification ref. The other fixes (Copilot/Claude mirror repointing, .serena/project.yml ignored_paths, mem-sentinel orphan sweep) are host-local/non-codebase changes not verifiable in the repo, and the one codebase-verifiable fix is absent.
findings.remediation: Merge Gerrit change 2725 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/2725) to land the removal of the [mcp_servers.serena] block from .codex/config.toml. Once merged, re-run verification to confirm the block is absent from the repository.
findings.title: Tracked .codex/config.toml serena entry not removed — Gerrit change 2725 not yet in working tree

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
